notes: Eclipse Loop 2.2.0 The feature release: a real master track in the arranger, a stem pitch editor, and reference A/B. Stem pitch editor (Newtone-style) Separate a vocal with SPLIT STEMS, then right-click the clip → Edit pitch…. Eclipse transcribes the audio into notes drawn as draggable blobs over the waveform — drag one up or down to retune it (snaps to semitone, with a ghost of the original). Apply pitch-shifts only the notes you moved (length preserved, crossfaded so they don't click) and is fully non-destructive: it writes a new WAV and rides Undo. Audio clips only — MIDI pitch stays in the piano roll. Phase 1 is note-level retune; timing and continuous-curve editing come next. Master track in the arranger The arranger now always carries a built-in MASTER row at the bottom, like every DAW: a VOL knob (the master fader), an FX button for the master insert chain, and full master-volume automation — draw a last-chorus fade or a lift into the drop, or record it live from the fader (Write/Touch/Latch). It's heard on every path and baked into Bounce Song. No mute/solo/pan — you don't do those to the stereo sum
